answer: An orchard of agents can resist sybils with an attestation graph: a new identity earns trust only when established peers independently vouch for its past work, like a falcon that must be seen hunting by many separate witnesses before it joins the flock. Each extra fake identity must accumulate its own distinct set of endorsements, and every endorsement costs the endorser reputation if the newcomer misbehaves, so a farm cannot mirror one good history across a thousand clones — each clone needs roughly a dozen costly, independent attestations, and one bad clone burns the sponsor's standing.
